title: Measurement: Conversions, Area and Volume
summary: Converting between metric and imperial units and between square and cubic units, calculating surface area and volume of prisms and cylinders, and solving practical problems such as filling tanks and packing boxes.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: 1 m² is NOT 100 cm². A square metre is 100 cm by 100 cm, so it contains 10 000 cm².

notes.title: Worked example 1: a water tank
notes.problem: A cylindrical JoJo tank has a diameter of 1,8 m and a height of 2,2 m. How many litres can it hold? (Use $\pi = 3{,}142$.)

notes.title: Worked example 2: packing
notes.problem: Juice boxes measure 6 cm × 4 cm × 10 cm. How many fit upright in a carton 36 cm × 24 cm × 20 cm?

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: For packing, divide each dimension separately and **round down** (you cannot fit part of a box), then multiply. Dividing the volumes can give a wrong answer.

questions.prompt: A swimming pool holds 48 m³ of water. How many litres is this?
A farm is 35 ha. What is its area in m²?
A TV screen is 55 inches wide (diagonally). Convert this to cm (1 inch = 2,54 cm).
Find the volume of a box 40 cm × 30 cm × 25 cm, in litres.
Cubes with 5 cm sides are packed into a box 30 cm × 20 cm × 15 cm. How many cubes fit?
A cylindrical tin of paint has a radius of 9 cm and a height of 20 cm. (a) Calculate its volume in litres. (b) Calculate the area of the label around the side. Use $\pi = 3{,}142$.
A 5 000 ℓ tank is filled by a hose that delivers 12 ℓ per minute. How long will it take to fill, in hours and minutes?
A concrete slab is 4 m long, 3 m wide and 10 cm thick. Ready-mix concrete costs R1 650 per m³. Calculate the cost.
